land.text: Caria and the Milas-Muğla country in south-western Anatolia

predecessors.note: The Menteshe page does not name a predecessor (it says only 'Founded in 1260/1290'); the Anatolian beyliks page says the beyliks of western Anatolia arose as Seljuk power was weakened after Köse Dağ (1243). Listed for continuity; no handover date on any page.

land.text: the Menteshe lands, 'incorporated into the Ottoman realm' in 1426

successors.note: Menteshe first submitted to the Ottomans in 1390 (Ottoman rule 1391-1402 on the ruler table), was restored after 1402, and recognised Ottoman overlordship in 1414 before the 1426 incorporation. Cliopatria's Ottoman shape covers Muğla from 1415.

capitals.name: Milas (Mylasa)
capitals.note: 'Its capital city was Milas (Mylasa) in southwestern Anatolia.' The page gives no years. It also names Beçin, Balat, Muğla and others as important centres; under the Ottomans the sanjak seat moved from Milas to Muğla (undated).

rulers.name: Menteshe Bey
rulers.note: Founder; the page's ruler table starts him in 1261 although the text says 'Founded in 1260/1290'.

rulers.name: Gazi Ahmed Bey
rulers.title: co-ruler
rulers.note: Ruler table then reads 'Ottoman rule 1391-1402'; the text dates the first submission to 1390.

rulers.name: Ilyas Bey
rulers.note: The table gives 1402-1424 (the strip follows it); the text says he recognised Ottoman overlordship in 1414 and that Menteshe was incorporated into the Ottoman realm in 1426, so the last two years have no listed ruler.

correction.text: the 1305 shape projected back to the founding: Milas and its country

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1305 but the page says 'Founded in 1260/1290' and the ruler table starts in 1261. The page gives no territory before 1305 (it notes that Aydın/Güzelhisar was held by the beylik for a time before passing to the Aydinids, undated), so the 1305 shape stands in; approximate.

correction.text: unchanged shape; it holds 1305-1389 only. Submission to Bayezid I in 1390 and Ottoman rule to 1402 follow

keyframe_review.note: Years only. 5,886 km2 covers Milas and Muğla; the page gives no area (so no infobox ratio), and its undated list of 'important centers' (Beçin, Milas, Balat, Elmalı, Finike, Kaş, Mağrı (Fethiye), Muğla, Çameli, Acıpayam, Tavas, Bozdoğan, Çine) reaches well beyond this core, so the shape is probably small for the beylik's greatest extent; the page does not date that extent. Cliopatria runs the shape to 1406 and ignores the 1390 submission and the 1391-1402 Ottoman rule.

correction.text: the restored beylik: the 1305 shape again from 1402

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'After 1402, Tamerlane restored the beylik to Menteşoğlu İlyas Bey' (ruler table Ilyas Bey 1402-1424). The restored extent is not given; the old core is used.

correction.text: unchanged shape; it holds to 1426, not 1414. From 1414 Ilyas Bey 'recognized Ottoman overlordship', so 1414-1426 is the Menteshe core as an Ottoman vassal

keyframe_review.note: Years and status only. Cliopatria ends the row in 1414 and its Ottoman shape takes Muğla in 1415; the page has the overlordship in 1414 and the incorporation 'a dozen years later, in 1426'. The Ottoman dossier should carry the vassal_start (1414) and vassal_end (1426) for this state.

ledger.note: 1261: Menteshe Bey founds the beylik, seated at Milas. The page says 'Founded in 1260/1290, it was named for its founder, Menteshe Bey' and its ruler table starts him in 1261; the Anatolian beyliks table gives 1261-1424. The page names the capital, not the extent; the region is Cliopatria's 1305 shape.

1390: Menteshe submits to Ottoman rule under Bayezid I. 'Menteşe Bey first submitted to Ottoman rule in 1390, during the reign of Bayezid I'; the ruler table shows 'Ottoman rule 1391-1402'. The page calls it submission, not conquest; a devastating earthquake had weakened the beylik in 1389.

1402: Timur restores Menteshe to Ilyas Bey. 'After 1402, Tamerlane restored the beylik to Menteşoğlu İlyas Bey'; the Battle of Ankara page dates the battle to July 1402 (the page does not mention the restoration). The Timurid dossier should carry the other side.

region.text: the whole beylik, a vassal since 1414

ledger.note: 1426: Menteshe is incorporated into the Ottoman realm. 'A dozen years later, in 1426, Menteshe was incorporated into the Ottoman realm.'

1426: the Menteshe beylik ends. The ruler table's Ilyas Bey 1402-1424 and the Anatolian beyliks table's '1261-1424' give 1424; the text says 1426. Ilyas Bey 'recognized Ottoman overlordship in 1414', so 1414-1426 is a vassalage.

wars.name: Menteshe raids on Rhodes
wars.outcome: No lasting gain: Mesut Bey 'briefly' conquered part of Rhodes in 1300; in 1311 a joint Genoese-Menteshe fleet attacked the Hospitallers on Rhodes 'but failed to capture the island'.
wars.note: Rhodes lies outside Cliopatria's Menteshe shape and the page names no holder in 1300, so no gain/loss is coded.

wars.name: Ottoman submission of Menteshe
wars.outcome: Menteshe Bey 'submitted to Ottoman rule' under Bayezid I; no fighting is described.
wars.note: Listed so that the reviewer can see it was considered; no contest is coded.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary; the beylik's limits (Aydinids to the north, Teke to the east, the Aegean coast) are approximate throughout.

sources.title: Menteshe
sources.note: Foundation, capital, ruler table, the 1300/1311 Rhodes episodes, 1389 earthquake, 1390 submission, restoration, 1414 overlordship, 1426 incorporation; no area, no infobox.

sources.title: Anatolian beyliks
sources.note: Table row: Menteşe, Menteşe Bey, Milas, 1261-1424; beyliks arising after Köse Dağ.

sources.title: Battle of Ankara
sources.note: Battle of Ankara dated July 1402 (context for the restoration; the page does not mention the beyliks).

notes: Two pages (Menteshe, Anatolian beyliks) plus the Battle of Ankara for the date. The page has no infobox and no area, so the 5,886 km2 shape could not be compared; its undated list of important centres (as far as Elmalı, Finike and Kaş) suggests a larger realm at some time. Cliopatria ends the row in 1414 and keeps one shape to 1406, ignoring the 1390 submission, the 1391-1402 Ottoman rule and the 1402 restoration; the dossier adds those as ledger events and new keyframes. End year: 1426 (text) against 1424 (ruler table, beyliks table). The 1414 vassalage has no event type on the vassal's side; the Ottoman dossier (me-10) should carry vassal_start 1414 and vassal_end 1426 with counterpart beylik-of-menteshe, and a gain from Menteshe in 1390 and 1426 mirroring the losses here. Timur's restoration should be mirrored by the Timurid dossier. Gazetteer: the place 'Milas' is missing (used only in capitals and text).
